_comment: Character overrides for the RS in-game-tone converter, keyed by REAL Rocksmith 2014 gear catalogue keys (Tones/tone_gear_data.json). Every key is validated against RsGearCatalog.Shared and the cab table must cover the ENTIRE catalogue — enforced by RsGearOverridesLivenessTests. Amps are not here: every amp the game ships converts through its own soundbank chain (`rsamp`, RsAmpChains, #88). Target ints use the NATIVE module semantics: cab model 0 = 1x12 clean / 1 = 2x12 / 2 = 4x12 scooped / 3 = vintage-dark (dcdsp_cab.h).

cabModel._comment: cab family stem (longest-prefix match of the cab Key, so every mic/position variant of a family resolves) -> the `cab` module's v24 ROSTER IR (0..25: 0 1x12 Combo, 1 2x12 Combo, 2 4x12 Scooped, 3 Vintage 4x12, 4 1x8 Tweed, 5 2x12 AC Open, 6 2x12 Boutique Closed, 7 4x12 Greenback, 8 4x12 V30 Modern, 9 4x10 Bass, 10 8x10 Bass Fridge, 11 1x15 Vintage Bass; and since 2026-10 (#74) the IRs built from measured driver responses: 12 4x10 Tweed Open, 13 1x10 Combo, 14 2x15 Guitar, 15 PA 15 + Horn, 16 PA Column, 17 Hi-Fi Tower, 18 2x10 Bass, 19 3x10 Bass, 20 6x10 Bass, 21 1x12 Bass, 22 2x12 Bass, 23 2x15 Bass, 24 4x15 Bass, 25 1x15 + 1x10 Bass). Picked by speaker layout first (count x size, open/closed back, read off the key and the game's own cabinet art in the game gear package), then era. Until 2026-10 only 0..3 were used and every bass cab rode the guitar 4x12. The mic and position in the key are a separate `micpos` layer (RsToneConverter.BuildCabMic). 'Bass_Cab_' stays as the catch-all for a bass cab this table does not name.

targetModule._comment: gear Key -> the module id this gear routes to when the generic category builder is not the right voice. Covers the drive family (fuzz / bigmuff / klon / rat / ds1 / hm2 / bassod), dynamics (limiter / multiband / optocomp / compressor), filters (svf / acousticsim / boost / bitcrusher / harmonizer: Pedal_BassEmulator is the game's Wwise Harmonizer), delays (bbddelay / multitap), reverbs (hallreverb), pitch (octfuzz) and modulation (ringmod). RsGearOverridesLivenessTests checks every key is real catalogue gear AND that the routed module is legal for that gear's category. Keys starting with '_' are ignored.
targetModule._comment09: 0.9 gear wave (native catalogue 57 -> 100). Every block below replaces a target that was an APPROXIMATION, or — for svf / acousticsim — a gear key the converter DROPPED. The per-knob maps live in the matching Build* method in RsToneConverter.cs.

staticParams._comment: gear Key -> { targetParamId: value } pinned unconditionally (converter clamps to the target range). The one remaining metal-zone-like gets a tight low end (Pedal_MetalDistortion moved to hm2, whose colour bells replace the pin); the one-off novelty cabs get their band-limited character.
